newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Absa gets strong credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Absa gets strong credit ratings.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) said on Tuesday that rating agency CA-Ratings had given it an AA mark for its ability to honour long-term debt and an A1 mark for short-term debt commitments.
Absa said the ratings compared well to similar international banks such National Australia Bank's AA rating and Royal bank of Canada's AA- rating.
"The organisation is of investment grade and that its capacity to meet long-term obligations in South African rand within South Africa is classed as very strong," the report said.
It added the A1 mark for short-term debt in rand within South Africa meant it was classed as "overwhelmingly strong".
The report said Absa's advances book is of a high quality and managed with a high degree of technical ability.

It added that the firm's information technology system is approaching self-sufficiency and that its managment had improved style and quality after coming under fire during a series of earlier retrenchment programmes.
However, the report said Absa's costs to total revenue ratio lagged behind those of rivals due to its proportionally lower non-interest income.
The report said Absa had to increase non-interest income by about 20 percent to be on a par with other similar South African banks.
CA-Ratings is an associate of Thomson Bank Watch -- the world's largest international bank's ratings agency.
